Diffusion of skills across professions by window

Source: R/emerging.R
compute_diffusion_panel.Rd

Counts the professions in which a skill has a revealed comparative advantage and measures how evenly the skill is spread over professions.

Usage

compute_diffusion_panel(
  rca,
  skill_col = "skill_id",
  prof_col,
  threshold = 1,
  compare = NULL
)

Arguments

rca

Output of compute_rca_panel().

skill_col

Skill column. Default "skill_id".

prof_col

Profession column.

threshold

RCA threshold. Default 1.

compare

Optional character vector of two window names, e.g. c("W1", "W3"). When given, the result has one row per skill with values of both windows and their differences.

Value

When compare = NULL, a data.table with skill_col, finestra, n_prof (professions with x > 0), n_prof_rca and entropia. Otherwise a data.table with skill_col, n_prof_rca_base, n_prof_rca_target, delta_n_prof_rca, entropia_base, entropia_target, delta_entropia, where base and target are the first and second element of compare; a skill absent from a window counts zero professions and zero entropy.

Details

For skill \(k\) in window \(W\), n_prof_rca is the number of professions with \(RCA_{kj} \ge\) threshold. With \(p_{kj} = s_{kj} / \sum_j s_{kj}\), the normalised entropy is \(H_k = -\sum_j p_{kj} \log p_{kj} / \log J\), where \(J\) is the number of professions present in the window. \(H_k = 1\) when the skill has the same share in all professions and 0 when it appears in one profession only.

Examples

panel <- data.table::data.table(
  cp4 = rep(c("p1", "p2"), each = 2), skill_id = rep(c("a", "b"), 2),
  mese_idx = 1, x = c(30, 5, 10, 20), n = rep(c(100, 100), each = 2)
)
rca <- compute_rca_panel(panel, prof_col = "cp4",
  windows = list(W1 = c(1, 1)))
compute_diffusion_panel(rca, prof_col = "cp4")
#>    skill_id finestra n_prof n_prof_rca  entropia
#>      <char>   <char>  <int>      <int>     <num>
#> 1:        a       W1      2          1 0.8112781
#> 2:        b       W1      2          1 0.7219281
